subject: Post-call: prompt collection + model recommendations for ACME (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: prompt collection + model recommendations for ACME (next steps)

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

- Goal: embed a multi-turn customer support assistant into ACME’s support portal (English, primary). Key constraints are latency under 600ms median, high factual accuracy on product config answers, and strict PII redaction.
- Workload: ~3.5k monthly active users, peak burst traffic during releases, typical prompt lengths 50–300 tokens.
- Risk areas you called out: hallucinations on product specs, edge cases with error logs, and sensitive customer identifiers in prompts.

Model fit / initial recommendations (based on our quick fit check):
- Redwood-Base-30B (quantized q4f) — best balance of accuracy and latency for long context; recommended for high-quality responses.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (optimized runtime) — good fallback for cost-sensitive paths.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — good for short-turn routing / low-latency microflows (e.g., quick triage).

I’ve shared a short benchmark overview from our internal evaluation here: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026-model-fit-report — this shows baseline accuracy and median latencies for a subset of your sample prompts.

Next steps we agreed on: 
1) You to share a prompt set (representative prompts + edge cases + any sample conversations). We can accept a spreadsheet or CSV. We prefer the schema in the attached prompt_collection_instructions.pdf and the redaction guidance template.
2) We’ll run a model-fit eval across the three recommended variants and return: per-prompt quality scores, latency P50/P95, token costs, and a short recommendation for a production model + rollout plan.
3) If you want, we’ll include an eval for automatic redaction/PII stripping and provide suggested in-prompt redaction transforms.

Attachments included: prompt_collection_instructions.pdf, redaction_guidance_template.csv

If possible, please upload the prompt set by end of week — that will let us get a preliminary eval back within 48–72 hours. If you prefer, you can paste 50–100 sample prompts directly into the body of a reply.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt collection + model recommendations for ACME (next steps)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and clear next steps. Attaching an initial sample set (acme_prompt_samples.csv) — ~120 rows covering:
- Typical support requests (account reset, billing questions)
- Product config questions (firmware/sensor parameters)
- Error log excerpts (we redacted customer IDs per our current process)
- Edge cases: ambiguous requests, chained questions, and truncated logs

A few clarifications / asks from our side: 
- For redaction: we currently mask customer_id and email, but there may still be free-text PII in logs. Any automated guidance you can provide (and whether you offer a sanitized ingestion pipeline) would be helpful.
- We’d like to know the expected evaluation turnaround and whether you’ll provide the per-prompt outputs (model responses) alongside quality annotations.

Also pasted below are three example prompts from the CSV for quick context: 

1) "Device X shows error code E-237 after firmware upgrade. What are the likely causes and first troubleshooting steps?"
2) "Customer A reports intermittent connectivity drop when device is behind NAT. They see logs: [redacted]. What additional logs should we collect?"
3) "List supported configuration flags for the sensor module and default values."

Let us know if you prefer the full CSV uploaded to the Drive or shared by SFTP.

—Sanjay
Head of Product, ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt collection + model recommendations for ACME (next steps)

Great — thanks for the CSV and sample prompts, Sanjay. That looks like a solid starting set. A few notes on process and what we’ll deliver: 

1) Ingestion & redaction options: 
- Quick path: you upload a redacted CSV (PII removed/masked) to the Drive link and we’ll run evals directly.
- Sanitized path: we can run an automated PII-scan/redaction pass on the raw CSV (we’ll need a signed data-processing scope) and return a sanitized copy plus an audit log. This is common when customers are unsure about embedded identifiers in logs.

2) What we’ll produce: 
- Per-prompt model outputs (for each candidate model variant) in a CSV, quality annotations (binary pass/fail + short comment), latency P50/P95, and token cost estimates.
- A short quality regression check vs. your baseline (if you provide baseline examples) and a recommended safe rollout plan (canary settings, threshold-based fallbacks to smaller model).

3) Model recommendations (more detail): 
- Redwood-Base-30B (q4f): target for initial production if accuracy/recall on product specs is primary. We’ll likely recommend quantized execution and a 2048 token window for your use case.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (opt): use as a lower-cost, slightly faster fallback for ephemeral prompts or webhooks.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: route very short triage flows; good for bursty microflows.

4) Quality regression concerns: 
- We’ll run an automated diff on a set of golden prompts to flag changes in answer structure or missing critical facts. If you have a small golden set (20–50 anchor prompts), include them in the upload.

5) Logistics: 
- Upload option: Drive link is easiest (see related_links). For the sanitized ingestion we’ll send a short data-processing email and an SFTP credential option.
- Timeline: once we have the CSV, we’ll run the initial eval within 48–72 hours and share the report.

I’ve attached prompt_collection_instructions.pdf and redaction_guidance_template.csv — the template has a recommended column schema (id, user_prompt, convo_history, expected_answer, tags, pii_marker).

Action for you: please either 1) upload the CSV to the Drive folder listed above, or 2) reply that you’d like the sanitized ingestion and we’ll send the secure intake link.

If both work, upload to Drive and we’ll start the eval tomorrow.

Thanks!
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On a related note, Nikhil — I’ll loop you into the Drive once the CSV is uploaded so you can kick off the automated eval in our internal console.
